settings.lede: We build trustworthy, privacy-preserving AI for connected systems: federated learning, edge intelligence, secure networks, quantum machine learning, causal AI and physical AI.
settings.mission: TrustNet.AI Lab studies how to make AI secure, private and dependable when it is trained and deployed across many devices, organizations and networks. Our work spans trustworthy federated learning, edge computing, post-quantum and blockchain security for vehicular networks, quantum machine learning, causal AI and physical AI.

people.bio: Asadullah Tariq is an Assistant Professor of AI and Robotics at New Uzbekistan University and a Postdoctoral Researcher at the College of Technological Innovation, Zayed University. He completed his PhD in Computing and Informatics at the United Arab Emirates University (2022 to 2025) with a thesis on a trustworthy federated learning framework for secure, efficient and quality-aware distributed AI, and was a visiting researcher at Queen Mary University of London. His research covers trustworthy and explainable AI, federated learning for wireless networks, quantum machine learning, edge computing, agentic AI and physical AI for communication networks.

people.name: Prof. Mohamed Adel Serhani
people.title: Professor and Dean, College of Computing and Informatics, University of Sharjah
people.bio: Mohamed Adel Serhani is Professor and Dean of the College of Computing and Informatics at the University of Sharjah. Before joining Sharjah, he was Assistant Dean for Research and Graduate Studies at the College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University (2018 to 2022), where he also directed the PhD and Master's programs. His research covers federated learning, cloud computing for data-intensive e-health applications, SLA enforcement in cloud data centres, the big data value chain, cloud federation and monitoring, and non-invasive smart health.
education: PhD Computer Engineering, Concordia University, Canada, 2006
MSc Software Engineering, University of Montreal, Canada, 2002

people.name: Prof. Irfan-ud Din
people.title: Professor and Head of Department of Computer Science, New Uzbekistan University
people.bio: Irfan-ud Din is Professor and Head of the Department of Computer Science at New Uzbekistan University in Tashkent. He previously served as Professor and Head of Computer Science at The Superior University Lahore, where he was also Director of ORIC (2021 to 2022), and as Associate Professor at INHA University in Tashkent (2015 to 2018). He held research and teaching posts at Incheon National University and Myongji University in South Korea, and was a postdoctoral researcher at KAIST. His research spans wireless communication, radio resource management, visible light communication and privacy-preserving federated learning.

people.name: Dr. Tariq Qayyum
people.title: Researcher, College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University
people.bio: Tariq Qayyum is a researcher at the College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University. His research covers federated learning, edge and fog computing, network security, cloud computing, the Internet of Things and distributed systems. His recent work includes decentralised hierarchical federated learning for privacy-aware fog computing, trustworthy split federated learning, quantum federated learning, and quantum-resilient blockchain for secure V2X networks.
education: PhD, College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University

people.name: Muhammad Ali
people.title: Lecturer, School of Computer and IT, Beaconhouse National University
people.bio: Muhammad Ali is a Lecturer at the School of Computer and Information Technology, Beaconhouse National University, Lahore, and a PhD scholar in Computer Science at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS). His research focuses on distributed systems, the Internet of Vehicles and edge computing, with work published in venues including the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics. He collaborates with the United Arab Emirates University on wireless communications and network systems research.
education: PhD Computer Science (in progress), Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS)
MS Information Technology, National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Pakistan

people.name: Dr. Ikbal Taleb
people.title: Assistant Professor, College of Technological Innovation, Zayed University
people.bio: Ikbal Taleb is an Assistant Professor at the College of Technological Innovation, Zayed University, in Abu Dhabi. He holds a PhD in Information and Systems Engineering from Concordia University and an MSc in Software Engineering from the University of Montreal, Canada. His research covers big data quality assessment and analytics, data-driven health applications, misinformation detection, and trustworthy and quantum federated learning.
education: PhD Information and Systems Engineering, Concordia University, Canada
MSc Software Engineering, University of Montreal, Canada

people.name: Dr. Muhammad Waqas Haseeb
people.title: Postdoctoral Researcher, Lund University and United Arab Emirates University
people.bio: Muhammad Waqas Haseeb is a Postdoctoral Researcher at Lund University and the United Arab Emirates University. His research brings together quantum mechanics and machine learning, including physics-informed neural networks, quantum state diffusion and open quantum systems, and quantum machine learning. His recent work includes a study of vibration-assisted electron tunnelling in COVID-19 infection using quantum state diffusion, and co-authored papers on quantum federated learning and quantum-enhanced convolutional neural networks for image classification.

people.name: Prof. Zouheir Trabelsi
people.title: Professor, Department of Information Systems and Security, College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University
people.bio: Zouheir Trabelsi is a Professor in the Department of Information Systems and Security at the College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University, where he chaired the Information Security department for seven years. He received his PhD in Computer Science from Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology, Japan, in 1994, and was a Fulbright Visiting Scholar. He has co-authored books on network security, including Network Attacks and Defenses: A Hands-on Approach, and his research covers network and information security, firewalls and intrusion detection, deep learning for cybersecurity, and post-quantum and blockchain security for vehicular networks and federated learning.
education: PhD Computer Science, Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology, Japan, 1994

Retractions, duplicates and newer published versions are flagged, and mistakes come back as a corrected .bib file. Everything runs in the browser, so nothing is uploaded or stored.

projects.summary: Trustworthy, privacy-preserving AI for monitoring and managing cardiovascular diseases.
projects.description: A Zayed University funded project developing an AI-driven framework for smart monitoring and management of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), building on the lab’s work in federated learning, digital twins and explainable edge intelligence for healthcare.

posts.title: Paper accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026
posts.summary: Our paper “Learning When to Communicate: Communication-Aware Physical AI with Digital Twins and Federated Mixture-of-Experts” has been accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 in Macau, China.
posts.body: Asadullah Tariq, Mohamed Adel Serhani, Tariq Qayyum and Ikbal Taleb show how physical AI agents can learn when it is worth communicating, combining digital twins with a federated mixture-of-experts to cut communication while keeping decisions accurate.

posts.title: Call for papers: FLAIRE-NextG workshop at IWCMC 2027, Barcelona
posts.summary: We are organising FLAIRE-NextG, a workshop on federated learning for AI-native, interpretable and resilient edge intelligence in NextG wireless networks, at IWCMC 2027 in Barcelona. Submissions close 15 January 2027.
posts.body:
Accepted papers will be submitted to IEEE Xplore, selected papers will be considered for five journal special issues, and there will be a best paper award.

See Workshops and special issues on this page for topics, dates and the submission link.

calls.title: Federated Learning for AI-native, Interpretable, and Resilient Edge Intelligence in NextG Wireless Networks
calls.host: IWCMC 2027 · 23rd International Wireless Communications & Mobile Computing Conference
calls.summary: FLAIRE-NextG brings together research on federated learning that is AI-native, interpretable and resilient for edge intelligence in NextG and 6G wireless networks, from causal and physics-informed FL to secure, auditable and trustworthy aggregation. IWCMC 2027 takes place 13 to 18 June 2027 in Barcelona, Spain.
calls.guidelines:
- Paper submission deadline: 15 January 2027
- Notification of acceptance: 30 March 2027
- Camera-ready submission: 30 April 2027
- Accepted papers will be submitted for inclusion in IEEE Xplore, subject to meeting its scope and quality requirements.
- Selected papers will be considered for publication in five journal special issues.
- There will be a best paper award.
